title: Connecticut Uniform Trust Code
summary: Connecticut Uniform Trust Code (CUTS) with Connecticut-specific modifications. Governs express trusts, charitable trusts, and fiduciary obligations. Contains significant nonuniform provisions compared to the model UTC, including explicit prohibition of self-settled spendthrift trusts.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Connecticut's CUTS has material departures from the model UTC; UTC-derived interpretations from other states may not apply.
Professional legal advice is required before applying Connecticut trust law.

title: Trust Creation, Validity, and Beneficiaries
summary: Connecticut trust creation requirements: intent, written instrument for land trusts, lawful purpose, ascertainable beneficiaries or charitable purpose, and trustee acceptance. Oral trusts for personal property are recognized subject to proof.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Capacity and undue influence issues require fact-specific analysis.
Statute of frauds requires written evidence for land trust claims.

title: Creditor Claim Rights Against Trusts
summary: Connecticut's CUTS creditor claim provisions. Governs reach of creditor claims against revocable and irrevocable trusts, spendthrift protections, exception creditors (support, government claims), and powers of withdrawal. Explicitly does NOT provide self-settled spendthrift protection.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Connecticut does not have a DAPT statute; self-settled trusts do NOT receive asset protection in Connecticut.
Support exception creditors may reach trust assets regardless of spendthrift clauses.

title: Trust Modification, Termination, and Reformation
summary: Connecticut trust modification and termination provisions. Covers nonjudicial settlement agreements, judicial modification, termination, and reformation. Requires court approval for many modifications; NJSA available for non-charitable trust modifications with interested party consent.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Charitable trust modifications require AG participation.
Court approval required for fundamental changes.

title: Directed Trusts
summary: Connecticut directed trust provisions. Authorizes trust instruments to designate a directed trustee, investment adviser, or distribution adviser. Defines fiduciary duties of directed trustees who follow permissible directions.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Following an improper direction may still result in directed trustee liability.
ERISA plan contexts may limit exculpation provisions.

title: Trust Protectors
summary: Connecticut trust protector provisions. Trust protectors may be appointed with powers including removing and appointing trustees, modifying trust terms, and directing trust investments. Protectors owe fiduciary duties unless exculpated by the trust instrument.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Exculpatory provisions in the trust instrument may limit protector liability.
Court may review protector actions for abuse.

title: Trust Decanting
summary: Connecticut trust decanting statute. Authorizes a trustee with power to make discretionary distributions to distribute trust assets to a second trust (decanting) for the benefit of beneficiaries, with notice requirements and court involvement for certain decanting actions.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Beneficiary and AG notice requirements apply.
Decanting that diminishes beneficiary interests may be challenged.

title: Trustee Duties, Powers, and Liabilities
summary: Connecticut trustee duties: loyalty, prudence, impartiality, administration costs, information to beneficiaries, accounting, and delegation. Covers trustee appointment, resignation, removal, and successor trustees.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Exculpatory clauses in trust instruments may limit but not eliminate liability for willful misconduct.
Prudent investor rule applies to entire trust portfolio.

title: Connecticut UCC Article 9
summary: Connecticut's adoption of Revised UCC Article 9. Governs secured transactions, financing statements, perfection, priority, and collateral enforcement. Connecticut Secretary of State is the central filing office for UCC liens.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Filing office acceptance does not establish attachment, enforceability, ownership, priority, or collateral validity.
Federal bankruptcy law may override state perfection and priority rules.

title: Connecticut Homestead Exemption
summary: Connecticut homestead exemption. Protects a debtor's primary residence from creditor execution, up to the statutory amount. Applies to natural persons and heads of household with specific income or age qualifications.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Statutory value cap applies; amounts above cap are not exempt.
Mortgages, tax liens, and certain government claims are not subject to the homestead exemption.

title: Governing Law and Principal Place of Administration
summary: Connecticut governing law and principal place of administration. Connecticut law governs if the trust instrument designates Connecticut as governing law, or if the trust is administered in Connecticut and the instrument is silent.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Other states' conflict-of-laws rules may determine governing law.
Federal courts may apply different choice-of-law analysis.

title: Revocable Trusts
summary: Connecticut revocable trust provisions. Settlor retains power to revoke, modify, or terminate a revocable trust during lifetime. Assets in a revocable trust are accessible to settlor's creditors during lifetime and to estate creditors at death.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Revocable trust assets are exposed to settlor's creditors during lifetime.
Post-death creditor claims against the estate may reach revocable trust assets.

title: Certification of Trust
summary: Connecticut trust certification provisions. A trustee may provide a written certification of trust (rather than the full trust instrument) to third parties. Certification must contain required elements; third parties relying on an accurate certification are protected.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
An inaccurate certification may result in trustee liability.
Omitting a material term limits the certification's legal effect.

title: Charitable Trusts and Cy Pres
summary: Connecticut charitable trust provisions. Governs creation, administration, and modification of charitable trusts. Includes cy pres for modifying charitable purposes when the original purpose becomes impracticable. Connecticut AG has oversight authority.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
AG involvement is required for charitable trust modifications.
Cy pres proceedings require court involvement.

citation: Connecticut Department of Revenue Services — Trust Tax Guidance
title: Connecticut Trust Income Tax
summary: Connecticut imposes an income tax on trusts with Connecticut nexus, including resident trusts and nonresident trusts with Connecticut source income. Filing thresholds and rates are governed by Connecticut tax statutes and DRS guidance.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Tax advice requires a licensed tax professional.
Connecticut estate tax remains in effect for larger estates.
Federal estate tax rules apply separately.

title: Combination and division of trusts
summary: Statutory basis for combining or dividing trusts.

title: Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by consent
summary: Governs modification/termination by consent.

title: Reformation to correct mistakes
summary: Authorizes court reformation to correct mistakes.

title: Removal of trustee
summary: Statutory grounds for trustee removal.

title: Co-trustees
summary: Governs decision making among co-trustees.

title: Duty of loyalty
summary: Codifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty.
